files.role: GET /review-stats/summary — the review-performance stats page's sole data endpoint. Module docstring states: real recorded review_events history only, three fixed rolling windows (day/week/month) in that order, scheduler-agnostic (aggregates across both Classic and FSRS, unlike backend/routers/experiment.py), no prior_review_interval filter (counts every completed review including rapid retries), recall_rate null (not 0) when a window has zero reviews.

public_objects.name: router
public_objects.purpose: APIRouter(prefix='/review-stats', tags=['review_stats']) — included by main.py under /api/essaycards, after experiment.router.

private_objects.name: REVIEW_STATS_SUMMARY_SCHEMA
private_objects.purpose: ColumnSchema list: period, reviews, unique_cards, again_count, hard_count, good_count, easy_count, failures, recall_rate. All sortable=False, filterable=False (fixed 3-row summary, not a data grid).

private_objects.name: _WINDOWS
private_objects.purpose: Ordered tuple of (period, interval_literal) pairs: ('day', '24 hours'), ('week', '7 days'), ('month', '30 days') — the single source of both the SQL window boundaries and the fixed output row order.

private_objects.name: _GRADES
private_objects.purpose: ('again', 'hard', 'good', 'easy') — the fixed grade vocabulary this endpoint's per-grade breakdown iterates over.

private_objects.name: _review_stats_aggregate
private_objects.purpose: Given cur: runs the single SQL statement described in 10_architecture.json internal_flow step 1 (one row of 18 filter(where ...) aggregates over essaycards.review_events, outer-restricted to the last 30 days) and returns it as one dict.

private_objects.name: _build_summary_rows
private_objects.purpose: Given the aggregate row dict: builds and returns the 3 row dicts (day, week, month, in that order) per internal_flow step 2, computing failures=again_count and recall_rate=(reviews-failures)/reviews if reviews>0 else None per window.

private_objects.name: _dataset_response
private_objects.purpose: Same pattern as the other routers' private helper of the same name — wraps a Dataset in a JSONResponse via model_dump(by_alias=True, mode='json').

files.role: FastAPI application entry point. This sprint: import backend.routers.review_stats and app.include_router(review_stats.router, prefix='/api/essaycards') after the existing seven app.include_router(...) calls (after experiment.router).

public_objects.name: app
public_objects.purpose: Router set gains review_stats.router this sprint, mounted last.

files.role: React entry point. This sprint: (1) a new ReviewStatsSummaryRow TS interface mirroring REVIEW_STATS_SUMMARY_SCHEMA (period: 'day' | 'week' | 'month', reviews, unique_cards, again_count, hard_count, good_count, easy_count, failures: number, recall_rate: number | null); (2) a new ReviewStatsView component fetching GET /essaycards/review-stats/summary on mount (apiFetch<Dataset<ReviewStatsSummaryRow>>/isApiError/ErrorCard/Skeleton, same convention as ExperimentDashboardView) and rendering three window cards; (3) a new Route for /stats.

public_objects.name: default
public_objects.purpose: Default export: Routes wiring gains <Route path="/stats" element={<ReviewStatsView />} />. Internal view/helper components (existing ones unchanged; new: ReviewStatsView) are not individually enumerated, per this file's established scaffold convention.

files.role: Add a top-level nav entry {id: 'essaycards-stats', label: 'Stats', path: '/essaycards/stats', order: 5} to both mobilePrimaryNav and desktopNav, immediately after the existing essaycards-experiment entry (order: 4) — same registration mechanism already used for every other top-level EssayCards view.

Add essaycards.review_events rows spanning: within-24h, within-7d-but-not-24h, within-30d-but-not-7d, and older-than-30d (must be excluded from every window) timestamps; a mix of grades including at least one 'again'; both scheduler='classic' and scheduler='fsrs' rows within the same window (scheduler-agnostic aggregation coverage); at least one row with a short prior_review_interval (rapid retry) to exercise the no-prior_review_interval-filter invariant. All new fixture ids prefixed fix- per existing convention. No existing fixture row's identity/timing is altered.

public_objects.name: test_review_stats_summary_returns_three_fixed_rows_in_order
public_objects.purpose: Scenario: Always three fixed rows in day/week/month order.

public_objects.name: test_review_stats_day_window_excludes_reviews_older_than_24_hours
public_objects.purpose: Scenario: Day window counts only reviews within the last 24 hours; week/month windows are wider and overlapping, not exclusive.

public_objects.name: test_review_stats_grade_breakdown_sums_to_reviews
public_objects.purpose: Scenario: Grade breakdown sums to reviews count; failures equals again_count.

public_objects.name: test_review_stats_recall_rate_is_null_when_window_has_zero_reviews
public_objects.purpose: Scenario: Recall rate is null (not 0) when a window has zero reviews.

public_objects.name: test_review_stats_recall_rate_computed_from_reviews_and_failures
public_objects.purpose: Scenario: Recall rate computed correctly when reviews exist.

public_objects.name: test_review_stats_aggregation_is_scheduler_agnostic
public_objects.purpose: Scenario: Aggregation combines classic and fsrs reviews with no per-scheduler breakdown in the response.

public_objects.name: test_review_stats_includes_rapid_retry_reviews
public_objects.purpose: Scenario: A review_events row with a short prior_review_interval (rapid retry) is still counted — no prior_review_interval filter, unlike GET /experiment/summary.
